title: Video upload
summary: Direct uploads to object storage, async transcoding and CDN delivery.

lesson.problem: Creators upload multi-gigabyte videos, and viewers around the world watch them on everything from phones to TVs.
why: Huge files should not flow through app servers. The upload API hands the client a pre-signed URL, and the client uploads straight to object storage, in resumable chunks.

The finished upload triggers a job. Transcoding workers convert the original into several resolutions and bitrates, split into short segments (HLS/DASH), so players can switch quality as bandwidth changes.
Processed segments are served through a CDN, which caches them close to viewers. The origin storage rarely sees viewer traffic.
takeaways: Keep large payloads off your servers: use pre-signed URLs and object storage.
Transcoding is slow and CPU-heavy, a natural fit for a queue and a worker fleet.
Video delivery is a CDN problem; storage is only the origin.
